svg.title: Multi-Agent Analysis
svg.desc: Proposed internal architecture for Multi-Agent Analysis in the Enterprise AI Agent Sales and Risk System. This is an architecture design drill-down, not evidence of a deployed multi-agent or background-job service. Scoped Inputs and Evidence starts with customer feedback from governed emails and meeting notes. Identity, customer, project, session and task scope are established by backend authorization, not by trusting customer-provided identifiers. AWS IAM covers AWS service permissions; Snowflake roles and application authorization enforce customer and project access. Scope and Access Check applies input screening and metadata validation before retrieval and reasoning. External documents and messages are treated as untrusted data, not executable instructions. Missing identity or required sources blocks analysis. Document Retrieval uses Cortex Search with backend identity-bound metadata filters or permission-scoped indexes. Cortex Search uses owner rights; source table row policies are not assumed to automatically isolate indexed results for every caller. Read-Only SQL tools use governed Snowflake views, parameterized approved queries, least-privileged credentials and enforced customer/project predicates. LLM-supplied SQL is not executed without validation. Financial values come from authoritative data and deterministic tools, not from semantic search alone. Delivery Risk Scores are previously computed ML batch outputs read from Snowflake score tables; they include model version, scoring timestamp, feature snapshot and freshness status. There is no foundation model retraining or ad hoc predictive-model invocation for every manager question. Evidence Snapshot records source identifiers, source versions, query identifiers, document excerpts, units, currencies, approved score versions and an as-of manifest. It checks compatibility across sources; it is not a distributed transaction guarantee. Stale, contradictory or missing critical data must be surfaced and may block a quote. Async Draft Generation submits a scoped job to an AWS SQS queue and immediately returns a job identifier to the UI. An application dispatcher consumes the queue and starts the worker on AWS Bedrock AgentCore Runtime; SQS does not automatically execute an AgentCore graph. Persisted job state tracks queued/running/failed/ready status. Bounded retry, dead-letter handling and idempotency keys prevent duplicate submissions or retries from publishing duplicate drafts. LangGraph implements the background workflow with a durable application checkpointer, not an in-memory session alone. The Async Draft Worker is application control flow, not a third autonomous business agent. It starts Business Agent and Engineering Agent from the same scoped evidence manifest, with independent outputs and deterministic state merges. Graph state contains scope, source versions, evidence references and structured outputs; role-specific excerpts are retrieved on demand under token, tool-call and time budgets. Enterprise-approved Bedrock models process the context. Business Agent interprets customer price feedback, commitments, commercial terms and margin constraints; it proposes negotiation alternatives supported by retrieved contracts, prior quotes, SQL facts and delivery-risk scores. Engineering Agent assesses technical feasibility, BOM and design-change impact, yield, tooling or test requirements, incremental costs and delivery implications. A risk score is a probability estimate, not a guarantee of an achievable date. The coordinator waits for both branches and reconciles assumptions and disagreements. Unresolved material conflicts are escalated for clarification; no arbitrary vote or unsupported consensus is treated as fact. Versioned Draft Quote Options combines the agents' outputs into versioned customer-specific alternatives. Application pricing tools calculate costs, prices, margins and scenario comparisons deterministically from source data and approved policies. The LLM writes explanations and cites evidence; it does not invent authoritative prices or approve discounts. Validation and Guardrails combines application numerical, customer, source, currency/unit, policy and version checks with AWS Bedrock Guardrails for applicable input/output screening. The visible output checkpoint is not the only validation step. The pytest mark denotes tested application rules, not a production pytest runner or a complete financial assurance product. Only checked options are committed to the Versioned Draft Store in Snowflake. Draft metadata includes customer/project, source manifest, calculation and graph versions, completion status and immutable revision/hash. A transactional conditional commit rejects late results from superseded jobs; the UI never treats an old or unfinished revision as ready for approval. Manager Chatbot loads the authorized draft through an authenticated backend connection in Streamlit in Snowflake. Managers compare options, ask evidence-backed follow-up questions and submit a selected version for review and approval. Manager Review and Approval selects an immutable option version and binds approver, customer/project, recipients or intended scope, content hash and source manifest. Manager authority is verified. Approved Quote Package is a reviewable artifact; no customer email or quote is sent automatically in this diagram. A later sending workflow must recheck freshness and scope. Question or Input Change is a backend-controlled route. Explanation/comparison questions reuse the current checked draft and its cited evidence; further authorized retrieval can occur if needed. New material facts route to recalculation, not a speculative answer from an outdated draft. Cost, order quantity or design-version changes are validated as authorized scenario inputs or verified source changes; a manager comment does not silently overwrite authoritative data. Recalculate Affected Steps resolves dirty nodes from a dependency map and enqueues a versioned revision job. It refreshes only relevant evidence and recomputes all dependent outputs: changed engineering costs may invalidate engineering analysis, pricing/margins, commercial options and validation; quantity changes may also affect capacity and delivery. Unchanged outputs are reused only when their complete input/dependency fingerprints match. Both agents are not blindly rerun for every chat turn. A scenario with incompatible or stale batch risk scores must obtain a valid score or show the limitation and block unsupported delivery commitments; changed scenarios do not imply retraining the risk model. The worker rechecks permissions and source versions before resuming affected nodes, runs numerical/policy validation, and publishes a new draft revision. Previous approvals become invalid for changed content or material source data. New revisions require manager review and approval again. Approval-time freshness checks prevent approval of superseded inputs, and a later sending workflow must validate the approved version and sources again. Feedback is a claim to verify, not automatic truth, and does not update model weights. Reviewed feedback and traces feed the separate Agent Evaluation and Observability module; telemetry and offline release-control arrows are abstracted here. LangGraph interrupt/resume with a durable application checkpointer supports review. Runtime session isolation is not a substitute for backend customer authorization or persistent approval records. Approval and checkpoint persistence are application infrastructure dependencies, beyond the visible draft store, omitted from this simplified view. Ollama remains a local inference alternative in the system overview; this drill-down shows the cloud Bedrock path to keep the model provider choice unambiguous. All visible text is English. Blue processing, grey validation and green manager-facing outcomes match the prior drill-downs. Brand marks retain native colors and consistent optical height. No business improvement metrics are claimed.
